reader_notes: Read by hand from the note text (dump.ts, bars 0-23), independently: no published analysis consulted. Motive searches were made with a throwaway contour script and every hit checked by reading the passage. x = the six sixteenths B A G F# G E (1:1.5-1:2.75: three steps down, a step up, a third down). y = the eighth-note countermotive that follows x in the right hand, B B E(dotted) F# D# (1:3-2:1.5); later it comes back only freely (dotted variants, e.g. C. B C. D at 10:1, G E C. C at 20:3, D# F# B. C A at 22:3). z = a dotted eighth followed by five sixteenths running down a scale (first at 3:3, C6 B A G F# E). The bass opens with a non-thematic octave leap on the tonic (E3 E2 at 1:1), a gesture it repeats before each of its x entries and at the cadences (V-V, I-I in octaves). No x-INV occurs.

opening.leader_meanwhile: free counterpoint: y (B B E. F# D#) against x in the bass; the bass does not go on to copy y (it plays octave eighths B3 B2 at 2:1), so it is head imitation, not canon
opening.notes: Bar 2 repeats the pattern a fifth higher: x on F# in the right hand (2:1.5, with D natural), x on F# in the bass two beats later (2:3.5, with D#: one note changed), the right hand meanwhile with a varied y (B5 A G F#. E F#). Bars 3-4 keep the same alternation (right hand x at beat 1.5, bass x at beat 3.5) but the bass now enters a twelfth below (x on B over x on E; x on A over x on D). The bass is non-thematic only for its first beat (E3 E2).

notes: The piece is made almost entirely of x: about thirty statements, always in its prime form, alternating between the hands (usually two beats apart) and carried through sequences; y is not a fixed countermotive and returns only as a rhythm. Only two segments recur as complete two-voice units, and both recurrences are varied: alpha (bars 1-2, recurring in D at 9:3 and soon aborted) and beta (the dominant-pedal figuration of 15:3-17, exchanged at the octave in 18-19). Unsure calls: (1) the member at 9:3 (perhaps only a statement of x with the opening's bass gesture); (2) the form: tripartite is chosen because sections 1 and 2 are equal (6 bars each) and section 2 begins with x in a new key (7:1.5), with the full opening layout following in D (9:3), but section 3 is longer (10 bars) and has no tonic return of the opening except x in the bass in the last cadence, so 'through-composed' is the alternative; (3) whether 15:3 counts as a half cadence; (4) the bass at 7:3.5 (G A B A B G) as a varied x. The cadence in D (9:3) is a local one inside section 2.
